title: Evolving Interdependent Operators with Large Language Models for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-based co-design of interdependent search operators for multi-objective evolutionary algorithms
mechanism.populationDetail: Multiple operator candidates are maintained in operator-specific collections; the MCTS tree stores partial design-thought strategies, not candidate-solution lineages, so it is not a second population structure.
mechanism.archiveDetail: Warm-start explicitly ranks and filters elite operators, which are analyzed and reused as code templates and design-thought material; precise archive size/retention is not given.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Operator rotation replaces one slot in the current multi-operator combination with the highest-fitness candidate; this does not specify survivor replacement in the maintained candidate operator populations.
mechanism.generationDetail: The LLM broadly redesigns one operator slot at a time using its prompt and current combination context, while MCTS composes thoughts across operator domains into a joint strategy; this is not multi-parent code fusion.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Aggregated multi-objective performance fitness updates MCTS statistics and guides operator replacement; textual design thoughts extracted from elite operators guide later generation.
mechanism.parentSelection: UCB recursively selects a child strategy node from the current MCTS tree; code-level source-parent selection is not otherwise specified.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: MCTS parent-child refers to search-tree strategy states. During operator rotation, one current operator slot is replaced; do not interpret the strategy tree as a genealogy tree of executable candidates.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Joint semantic co-design of interdependent operator-thought tuples followed by sequential operator-slot rotation is not fully captured by single-candidate modification labels.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/Evolving Interdependent Operators with Large Language Models for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The MCTS tree stores partial design-thought tuples rather than executable candidate lineages; Chapter 3 tree placement needs this qualification. Candidate-pool replacement and ordinary code-parent selection are underspecified. Multi-thought strategy composition is not code-level multi-parent fusion.
